tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches

schema.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A proposal the user already started, dismissed or let expire is reported back (a dismissed or expired proposal's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
tools.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.
Right before calling, write its bold title line and one sentence on what it will do; it has started only once this returns saying so. Never wait for it or poll.

"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work: the user follows your progress by it and will never ask for it, so it is part of the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

content.description: The step, as a short imperative phrase (≤7 words).

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list. Use on the first call and whenever the plan changes.

advance.description: true: the in_progress step is done and the next pending step starts (the cheap, usual update).

done.description: 1-based numbers of steps just completed (out-of-order updates).

start.description: 1-based number of the step now in progress (with done, for out-of-order updates).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

"""Planning Grid view (CSS Grid + Excel-like editing via ExcelGrid)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons.components.dialogs import delete_dialog
from alloq_commons.components.excel_grid import grid_row_attrs
from alloq_commons.components.formatters import de_number, match_str
from alloq_commons.components.forms import quick_project_fields, section
from alloq_commons.components.modal_layout import (
    MODAL_CLASS,
    modal_footer,
    modal_form_layout,
)
from alloq_project.components.planning_shared import (
    CELL_BASE,
    CURRENT_WEEK_BG,
    EMP_HEADER_BG,
    LABEL_CELL_BASE,
    STICKY_BLOCK_HEADER,
    STICKY_LEFT_BODY,
    STICKY_LEFT_EMP_HEADER,
    STICKY_LEFT_GESAMT,
    block_header_info_cell,
    current_week_bg,
    editable_value_cell,
    empty_grid_row,
    format_de,
    format_gesamt,
    grid_row,
    header_block,
    planning_excel_grid,
    summary_stat,
)
from alloq_project.states.planning_absence_state import PlanningAbsenceState
from alloq_project.states.planning_grid_state import (
    EmployeeBlock,
    GesamtCell,
    GridCell,
    PlanningStore,
    ProjectAllocationRow,
)
from alloq_team.components.employee import absence_modal
from alloq_team.states.team_state import TeamState
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gesamt bucket styling (employee-specific)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _gesamt_color(bucket: rx.Var[str]) -> rx.Var[str]:
    return match_str(
        bucket,
        (
            "over",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-red-7), var(--mantine-color-red-3))",
        ),
        (
            "tight",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-violet-7), var(--mantine-color-violet-3))",
        ),
        (
            "available",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-green-7), var(--mantine-color-green-3))",
        ),
        (
            "balanced",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-green-6), var(--mantine-color-green-4))",
        ),
        (
            "absent",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-blue-7), var(--mantine-color-blue-3))",
        ),
        "var(--alloq-text)",
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Employee block
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _employee_header_row(emp: ObjectVar[EmployeeBlock]) -> rx.Component:
    is_collapsed = PlanningStore.collapsed_employees.contains(emp.id)
    return grid_row(
        mn.box(
            mn.group(
                mn.group(
                    mn.action_icon(
                        rx.cond(
                            is_collapsed,
                            rx.icon("chevron-right", size=16, stroke_width=2),
                            rx.icon("chevron-down", size=16, stroke_width=2),
                        ),
                        variant="subtle",
                        color="gray",
                        size="sm",
                        on_click=PlanningStore.toggle_employee(emp.id),  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
                    ),
                    mn.text(
                        emp.last_name + ", " + emp.first_name,
                        size="sm",
                        fw="700",
                        c="var(--alloq-text)",
                    ),
                    gap="sm",
                    align="center",
                    wrap="nowrap",
                ),
                de_number(
                    emp.hours_per_week,
                    suffix="h/W",
                    size="xs",
                    c="var(--alloq-text-muted)",
                    fw="400",
                ),
                justify="space-between",
                align="center",
                wrap="nowrap",
                w="100%",
            ),
            style={
                **LABEL_CELL_BASE,
                **STICKY_LEFT_EMP_HEADER,
                "borderTop": "1px solid var(--alloq-border-strong)",
                "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border-strong)",
            },
        ),
        block_header_info_cell(
            mn.group(
                mn.tooltip(
                    mn.action_icon(
                        rx.icon("calendar-plus", size=14, stroke_width=2),
                        variant="subtle",
                        color="gray",
                        size="xs",
                        aria_label="Abwesenheit eintragen",
                        on_click=TeamState.select_employee_and_add_absence(  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
                            emp.real_id,
                        ),
                    ),
                    label="Abwesenheit eintragen",
                ),
                mn.tooltip(
                    mn.action_icon(
                        rx.icon("plus", size=14, stroke_width=2),
                        variant="subtle",
                        color="gray",
                        size="xs",
                        aria_label="Projekt zuweisen",
                        on_click=PlanningStore.open_add_project_for_employee(  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
                            emp.id,
                        ),
                    ),
                    label="Projekt zuweisen",
                ),
                gap="xs",
                wrap="nowrap",
            ),
            summary_stat("Geplant", emp.planned_days),
            summary_stat("Verfügbar", emp.available_days),
            background=EMP_HEADER_BG,
        ),
        style=STICKY_BLOCK_HEADER,
    )


def _project_label_cell(project: ObjectVar[ProjectAllocationRow]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        mn.group(
            mn.box(
                style={
                    "width": "4px",
                    "height": "20px",
                    "borderRadius": "2px",
                    "backgroundColor": project.color,
                    "flexShrink": "0",
                },
            ),
            mn.text(
                project.name,
                size="sm",
                c="var(--alloq-text)",
                truncate=True,
                flex="1",
                style={"minWidth": 0},
            ),
            rx.cond(
                project.role_short != "",
                mn.badge(
                    project.role_short,
                    size="xs",
                    radius="sm",
                    variant="filled",
                    color=project.role_color,
                    c="var(--alloq-text)",
                    fw="700",
                ),
                rx.fragment(),
            ),
            mn.tooltip(
                delete_dialog(
                    title="Projektzuweisung entfernen",
                    content=f"{project.code} — {project.name}",
                    on_click=PlanningStore.remove_project_from_employee_grid(  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
                        project.emp_id, project.real_project_id
                    ),
                    icon_button=True,
                    color="red",
                    size="xs",
                    variant="subtle",
                ),
                label="Projekt entfernen",
            ),
            gap="sm",
            align="center",
            justify="space-between",
            wrap="nowrap",
            w="100%",
        ),
        style={
            **LABEL_CELL_BASE,
            **STICKY_LEFT_BODY,
            "paddingLeft": "16px",
        },
    )


def _project_row_view(project: ObjectVar[ProjectAllocationRow]) -> rx.Component:
    return grid_row(
        _project_label_cell(project),
        rx.foreach(project.cells, editable_value_cell),
        attrs=grid_row_attrs(f"{project.emp_id}|{project.code}", project.emp_id),
    )


def _absence_value_cell(cell: ObjectVar[GridCell]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        rx.cond(
            cell.value.to(float) > 0,
            mn.text(
                format_de(cell.value),
                size="xs",
                c="var(--alloq-text-muted)",
            ),
            mn.text("", size="xs"),
        ),
        style={
            **CELL_BASE,
            "color": "var(--alloq-text-muted)",
            "backgroundColor": current_week_bg(cell.week_key),
        },
    )


def _absence_row(emp: ObjectVar[EmployeeBlock]) -> rx.Component:
    return grid_row(
        mn.box(
            mn.text("Abwesenheit", size="xs", c="var(--alloq-text-muted)"),
            style={
                **LABEL_CELL_BASE,
                **STICKY_LEFT_BODY,
                "paddingLeft": "16px",
            },
        ),
        rx.foreach(emp.absence.cells, _absence_value_cell),
    )


def _internal_value_cell(cell: ObjectVar[GridCell]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        rx.cond(
            cell.value.to(float) > 0,
            mn.text(
                format_de(cell.value),
                size="xs",
                c="var(--alloq-text-muted)",
            ),
            mn.text("", size="xs"),
        ),
        style={
            **CELL_BASE,
            "color": "var(--alloq-text-muted)",
            "backgroundColor": current_week_bg(cell.week_key),
        },
    )


def _internal_row(emp: ObjectVar[EmployeeBlock]) -> rx.Component:
    return grid_row(
        mn.box(
            mn.text("Interne Projekte", size="xs", c="var(--alloq-text-muted)"),
            style={
                **LABEL_CELL_BASE,
                **STICKY_LEFT_BODY,
                "paddingLeft": "16px",
            },
        ),
        rx.foreach(emp.internal.cells, _internal_value_cell),
    )


def _gesamt_value_cell(cell: ObjectVar[GesamtCell]) -> rx.Component:
    is_current = cell.week_key == PlanningStore.current_week_key
    return mn.box(
        format_gesamt(cell.value),
        style={
            **CELL_BASE,
            "backgroundImage": rx.cond(
                is_current,
                f"linear-gradient({CURRENT_WEEK_BG}, {CURRENT_WEEK_BG})",
                "none",
            ),
            "color": _gesamt_color(cell.bucket),
            "fontWeight": "600",
            "fontSize": "11px",
        },
    )


def _gesamt_row(emp: ObjectVar[EmployeeBlock]) -> rx.Component:
    return grid_row(
        mn.box(
            mn.text("Gesamt (frei)", size="12px", fw="700", c="var(--alloq-text)"),
            style={
                **LABEL_CELL_BASE,
                **STICKY_LEFT_GESAMT,
            },
        ),
        rx.foreach(emp.gesamt, _gesamt_value_cell),
    )


def _employee_block(emp: ObjectVar[EmployeeBlock]) -> rx.Component:
    is_collapsed = PlanningStore.collapsed_employees.contains(emp.id)
    return mn.box(
        _employee_header_row(emp),
        rx.cond(
            ~is_collapsed,
            mn.box(
                rx.foreach(emp.projects, _project_row_view),
                rx.cond(
                    ~PlanningStore.hide_internal,
                    rx.fragment(_internal_row(emp), _absence_row(emp)),
                    rx.fragment(),
                ),
                _gesamt_row(emp),
                empty_grid_row(),
            ),
            rx.fragment(),
        ),
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Add project modal
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _add_project_modal() -> rx.Component:
    """Modal to assign a project to an employee from the grid."""
    return mn.modal(
        modal_form_layout(
            content=mn.flex(
                section(
                    mn.select(
                        name="project_id",
                        label="Projekt",
                        data=PlanningStore.add_project_options.to(list[dict[str, Any]]),
                        value=PlanningStore.add_project_selected,
                        on_change=PlanningStore.set_add_project_selected,
                        required=True,
                        searchable=True,
                        clearable=True,
                        left_section=rx.icon("folder", size=16),
                    ),
                    rx.cond(
                        PlanningStore.quick_create_active,
                        quick_project_fields(
                            name_value=PlanningStore.quick_project_name,
                            on_name_change=PlanningStore.set_quick_project_name,
                            code_value=PlanningStore.quick_project_code,
                            on_code_change=PlanningStore.set_quick_project_code,
                            on_create=PlanningStore.quick_create_project,
                            loading=PlanningStore.is_quick_creating,
                        ),
                        rx.fragment(),
                    ),
                    mn.select(
                        name="role_id",
                        label="Rolle",
                        data=PlanningStore.add_project_role_options.to(
                            list[dict[str, str]]
                        ),
                        required=True,
                        searchable=True,
                        clearable=True,
                        left_section=rx.icon("shield", size=16),
                    ),
                ),
                mn.space(height="2rem"),
                direction="column",
                gap="md",
                width="100%",
            ),
            footer=modal_footer(
                "Zuweisen",
                PlanningStore.close_add_project_for_employee,
            ),
            on_submit=PlanningStore.add_project_to_employee_grid,
            reset_on_submit=True,
        ),
        title="Projekt zuweisen",
        opened=PlanningStore.add_project_emp_id != "",
        on_close=PlanningStore.close_add_project_for_employee,
        size="md",
        centered=True,
        z_index=300,
        class_name=MODAL_CLASS,
        overlay_props={"backgroundOpacity": 0.5, "blur": 4},
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main component
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def planning_grid() -> rx.Component:
    return rx.fragment(

"""Shared constants, styles, and components for planning grid views."""

from __future__ import annotations

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons.components.excel_grid import excel_grid, grid_cell_attrs
from alloq_commons.components.formatters import de_number
from alloq_commons.components.list_view import sticky_block_header
from alloq_project.states.planning_grid_state import (
    LABEL_COL_PX,
    WEEK_COL_PX,
    GridCell,
    MonthSpan,
    PlanningStore,
    WeekColumn,
)
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dimension constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

LABEL_COL_WIDTH = f"{LABEL_COL_PX}px"
WEEK_COL_WIDTH = f"{WEEK_COL_PX}px"
ROW_HEIGHT = "32px"
HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT = "30px"
MONTH_HEADER_BG = "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-blue-0), var(--mantine-color-blue-9))"

CURRENT_WEEK_BG = "var(--aq-now)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Style dictionaries
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

GRID_WRAPPER_STYLE = {
    "backgroundColor": "var(--aq-surface)",
    "overflow": "auto",
    "flex": "1",
    "minHeight": "0",
    "width": "100%",
}
"""Fills the content pane below the scope bar and scrolls both ways."""

ROW_STYLE_BASE = {
    "display": "grid",
    "alignItems": "stretch",
}

CELL_BASE = {
    "display": "flex",
    "alignItems": "center",
    "justifyContent": "center",
    "padding": "0 4px",
    "fontSize": "0.8125rem",
    "color": "var(--alloq-text)",
    "borderRight": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
    "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
    "minHeight": ROW_HEIGHT,
    "fontVariantNumeric": "tabular-nums",
}

LABEL_CELL_BASE = {
    **CELL_BASE,
    "justifyContent": "flex-start",
    "padding": "0 12px",
    "minWidth": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
    "width": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
}

STICKY_LEFT_BODY = {
    "position": "sticky",
    "left": "0",
    "zIndex": "2",
    "backgroundColor": "var(--alloq-surface-solid)",
}

STICKY_LEFT_HEADER_TOP = {
    "position": "sticky",
    "left": "0",
    "zIndex": "50",
    "backgroundColor": MONTH_HEADER_BG,
}

STICKY_LEFT_HEADER = {
    "position": "sticky",
    "left": "0",
    "zIndex": "50",
    "backgroundColor": "var(--alloq-surface-muted)",
}

STICKY_LEFT_GESAMT = {
    "position": "sticky",
    "left": "0",
    "zIndex": "2",
    "backgroundColor": "var(--alloq-surface-muted)",
}

STICKY_LEFT_EMP_HEADER = {
    "position": "sticky",
    "left": "0",
    "zIndex": "2",
    "backgroundColor": "var(--alloq-surface-hover)",
}

STICKY_BLOCK_HEADER = sticky_block_header("90px")

HEADER_BLOCK_STYLE = {
    "position": "sticky",
    "top": "0",
    "zIndex": "30",
    "backgroundColor": "var(--alloq-surface-muted)",
}

EMP_HEADER_BG = "var(--alloq-surface-hover)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared helper functions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def current_week_bg(
    week_key: rx.Var[str], fallback: str = "transparent"
) -> rx.Var[str]:
    """Return background color highlighting the current week."""
    return rx.cond(
        week_key == PlanningStore.current_week_key, CURRENT_WEEK_BG, fallback
    )


def grid_row(
    *children: rx.Component,
    style: dict | None = None,
    attrs: dict | None = None,
) -> rx.Component:
    """A single CSS grid row bound to PlanningStore columns."""
    return mn.box(
        *children,
        custom_attrs=attrs or {},
        style={
            **ROW_STYLE_BASE,
            "gridTemplateColumns": PlanningStore.grid_template_columns,
            "minWidth": PlanningStore.table_width,
            "width": PlanningStore.table_width,
            **(style or {}),
        },
    )


def empty_grid_row() -> rx.Component:
    """A full-width blank planning row with no cells."""
    return grid_row(style={"height": ROW_HEIGHT})


def format_de(value: rx.Var[float] | float) -> rx.Component:
    """Format a number in German locale; show blank for zero."""
    return rx.cond(
        value == 0,
        mn.box(""),
        de_number(
            value=value,
            decimal_scale=2,
            minimum_fraction_digits=2,
            fixed_decimal_scale=True,
        ),
    )


def format_gesamt(value: rx.Var[float]) -> rx.Component:
    """Format a Gesamt (total) number — always displayed."""
    return de_number(
        value=value,
        decimal_scale=2,
        minimum_fraction_digits=2,
        fixed_decimal_scale=True,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Block header info (pinned beside the label column)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY_TOOLTIP = "Ab der aktuellen Woche bis zum Ende des Zeitraums"


def summary_stat(label: str, value: rx.Var[float]) -> rx.Component:
    """Muted label followed by a person-day figure."""
    return mn.group(
        mn.text(label, size="xs", c="var(--alloq-text-muted)"),
        mn.text(
            de_number(
                value=value,
                decimal_scale=2,
                fixed_decimal_scale=True,
                suffix=" PT",
            ),
            size="xs",
            fw="600",
            c="var(--alloq-text)",
        ),
        gap="4px",
        align="center",
        wrap="nowrap",
    )


def block_header_info_cell(*children: rx.Component, background: str) -> rx.Component:
    """Week-column part of a block header; its content stays horizontally pinned."""
    return mn.box(
        mn.tooltip(
            mn.group(
                *children,
                gap="md",
                align="center",
                wrap="nowrap",
                style={
                    "position": "sticky",
                    "left": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
                    "padding": "0 12px",
                },
            ),
            label=SUMMARY_TOOLTIP,
            open_delay=400,
        ),
        style={
            **CELL_BASE,
            "gridColumn": "2 / -1",
            "justifyContent": "flex-start",
            "padding": "0",
            "backgroundColor": background,
            "borderTop": "1px solid var(--alloq-border-strong)",
            "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border-strong)",
            "borderRight": "none",
        },
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared header components
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def month_cell(month: ObjectVar[MonthSpan]) -> rx.Component:
    """Header cell spanning one month."""
    return mn.box(
        mn.text(month.label, fz="11px", fw="700", c="var(--alloq-text)"),
        style={
            **CELL_BASE,
            "gridColumn": "span " + month.span.to_string(),
            "position": "relative",
            "zIndex": "0",
            "backgroundColor": MONTH_HEADER_BG,
            "fontWeight": "500",
            "justifyContent": "flex-start",
            "paddingLeft": "12px",
            "minHeight": HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
        },
    )


def week_label_cell(week: ObjectVar[WeekColumn]) -> rx.Component:
    """Header cell for a week number."""
    return mn.box(
        mn.text(week.label, fz="11px", c="var(--alloq-text-muted)", fw="500"),
        style={
            **CELL_BASE,
            "position": "relative",
            "zIndex": "0",
            "minHeight": HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
            "backgroundColor": current_week_bg(week.key, "var(--alloq-surface-muted)"),
            "fontWeight": "500",
        },
    )


def work_days_cell(week: ObjectVar[WeekColumn]) -> rx.Component:
    """Header cell showing work days per week."""
    return mn.box(
        format_de(week.work_days),
        style={
            **CELL_BASE,
            "position": "relative",
            "zIndex": "0",
            "minHeight": HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
            "backgroundColor": current_week_bg(week.key, "var(--alloq-surface-muted)"),
            "fontWeight": "500",
            "fontSize": "11px",
            "borderBottom": "2px solid var(--alloq-border-strong)",
        },
    )


def label_th(text: str, *, accent: bool = False, last: bool = False) -> rx.Component:
    """Sticky label header cell."""
    sticky = STICKY_LEFT_HEADER_TOP if accent else STICKY_LEFT_HEADER
    extra = {"borderBottom": "2px solid var(--alloq-border-strong)"} if last else {}
    return mn.box(
        mn.text(text, size="xs", fw="700", c="var(--alloq-text)"),
        style={
            **LABEL_CELL_BASE,
            **sticky,
            **extra,
            "minHeight": HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
        },
    )


def header_block() -> rx.Component:
    """Three-row header: months, weeks, work days."""
    return mn.box(
        grid_row(
            label_th("Monat", accent=True),
            rx.foreach(PlanningStore.month_spans, month_cell),
        ),
        grid_row(
            label_th("Woche"),
            rx.foreach(PlanningStore.weeks, week_label_cell),
        ),
        grid_row(
            label_th("Arbeitstage (brutto)", last=True),
            rx.foreach(PlanningStore.weeks, work_days_cell),
        ),
        style=HEADER_BLOCK_STYLE,
        custom_attrs={"data-grid-header": "true"},
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared value cell (selection/editing handled by ExcelGrid)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

GRID_ROOT_STYLE = {**GRID_WRAPPER_STYLE, "outline": "none"}


def planning_excel_grid(*children: rx.Component, grid_id: str) -> rx.Component:
    """Excel-like interaction layer bound to PlanningStore."""
    return excel_grid(
        *children,
        id=grid_id,
        grid_label="Kapazitätsplanung",
        revision=PlanningStore.grid_revision,
        dirty=PlanningStore.has_dirty,
        saving=PlanningStore.is_saving,

# Planning Grid: readability rework (refined prompt)

## Context

The resource planning grid (`view_mode == "Grid"`, employee blocks × weeks) shows every
value as a bold-ish `5,00` in a fully ruled grid. With 4 employees and 13 weeks the user
already sees ~250 numbers, most of them identical. Users cannot spot what matters
(overbooking, free capacity, holidays, absences). Goal: the grid stays Excel-editable,
but the eye goes to exceptions first and the repetitive values fade into the background.

User decisions (confirmed):
- Scope: full rework incl. new display modes and density.
- Keep fixed 2 decimals (`5,00`, `0,50`).
- Gesamt row emphasises only exceptions.

---

## Part A — Analysis: what makes the current grid hard to read

Based on established guidance for number-heavy tables (Tufte data-ink ratio; Stephen Few
"Show Me the Numbers" table design; Excel conditional formatting / data bars; resource
planners like Float, Runn, Resource Guru; WCAG 1.4.1 "use of color").

| # | Problem in screenshot | Principle violated | Fix direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Long runs of identical `5,00` per project row; the run's *shape* (start, end, gaps) is the information, not each number | Redundant data ink; preattentive shape beats reading | Data bars / run visualization; repeated values de-emphasised |
| 2 | Every cell has right + bottom border → heavy cage | Non-data ink; gridlines should be barely visible | Drop vertical cell borders, keep faint horizontal lines, stronger month separator only |
| 3 | Numbers centered | Numbers must be right-aligned with tabular figures so decimals line up | Right-align all numeric cells (`tabular-nums` already set) |
| 4 | `Interne Projekte 0,50` repeated in every week for every employee | Constant values carry no information | Show only deviations from the employee's default, or hide by default; fold into Gesamt tooltip |
| 5 | `Arbeitstage (brutto)` header row shows `5,00` 11 times, only holiday weeks matter | Same as 4 | Show only non-standard weeks (e.g. `3,00` highlighted), blank otherwise; or a holiday marker in the week header |
| 6 | Gesamt uses 6 colours (red, violet, 2 greens, blue, black) | Too many hues; no clear meaning | One diverging scheme: red = overbooked, neutral = fully booked, green = free |
| 7 | `absent` bucket paints the value blue even when it is **overbooked** (`-6,50`, `-2,60` blue) | Colour hides the most important exception | Colour from free value only; absence shown separately (icon / hatching in the absence row) |
| 8 | Fully booked weeks `0,00` are bold black → the *ideal* state is the most prominent | Emphasis on the non-exception | Render `0,00` muted (or `✓`/`–`), bold only for exceptions |
| 9 | Signed numbers rely on colour alone (red vs green) | WCAG 1.4.1 | Keep the sign, add a tinted cell background for overbooked cells; tooltip with breakdown |
| 10 | Mixed font sizes (13 px values, 12 px internal, 11 px Gesamt, 11 px headers) | Inconsistent hierarchy | 2 sizes: values 13 px, secondary 12 px; hierarchy via weight/colour, not size |
| 11 | Header summary "Verfügbar 18,50 PT" next to a row full of `-5,50` | Conflicting messages | Header shows exception summary: "Überbucht 44,00 PT in 8 Wo." / "Frei 18,50 PT" |
| 12 | Collapsed employee shows nothing in the week columns | Lost overview | Collapsed header row shows the Gesamt cells inline → one line per person = team overview |
| 13 | 32 px blank spacer row between blocks | Wasted vertical space | 8–12 px gap; block separation via a stronger top border |
| 14 | Week labels `5.10.` without KW | Planners think in KW | Optional `KW 41` with date in tooltip |

Key takeaway: **encode the routine as shape and faint text, encode the exceptions as
colour and weight.** The number is always available (selection, tooltip, edit), but it
does not have to shout in every cell.

---

## Part B — Implementation prompt

### Task
Rework the visual presentation of the employee planning grid
(`components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/components/planning_grid.py`) and its shared
pieces (`planning_shared.py`) so repetitive values recede and exceptions stand out. Add a
**display mode** switch (Zahlen / Balken) and a **density** switch (Kompakt / Normal),
both persisted per browser. Excel-like editing (`ExcelGrid`) must keep working in all
modes. Apply the shared styling also to the project view (`planning_project_view.py`)
where the same helpers are used.

### Context (existing code to reuse)
- Cells and styles: `planning_shared.py` — `CELL_BASE`, `LABEL_CELL_BASE`, `format_de`,
  `format_gesamt`, `editable_value_cell`, `work_days_cell`, `week_label_cell`,
  `summary_stat`, `block_header_info_cell`, `empty_grid_row`, `current_week_bg`.
- Employee block rendering: `planning_grid.py` — `_employee_header_row`,
  `_project_row_view`, `_internal_row`, `_absence_row`, `_gesamt_row`, `_gesamt_color`.
- Gesamt buckets: `UtilizationService.gesamt_bucket` / `compute_employee_gesamt` in
  `components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/services/utilization.py:149` and `:288`
  (`absent` overrides the free-value bucket — this is bug #7).
- Builders: `compute_gesamt`, `employee_summary` in
  `components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/services/planning_builders.py`.
- Models: `GridCell`, `GesamtCell`, `EmployeeBlock` in `states/planning_models.py`;
  `WEEK_COL_PX=60`, `LABEL_COL_PX=300`.
- Editing layer: `components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/excel_grid/excel_grid.jsx`
  needs `data-row-key` / `data-cell-key` / `data-col` / `data-value` on editable cells
  (`grid_row_attrs`, `grid_cell_attrs`). Do **not** change these contracts.
- Persisted UI prefs pattern: `rx.LocalStorage(...)` as in
  `states/project_list_state.py:84`.
- Existing heatmap view (`planning_heatmap.py`) already shows utilization %; do not
  duplicate it.
- `states/planning_grid_state.py` is already **1037 lines** (> 1000 limit). New state
  goes into a **mixin** (see memory "Reflex mixin, not substate"), e.g.
  `states/planning_display_mixin.py`, not into the store file.

### Requirements

**R1 Numbers & alignment**
1. Keep fixed 2 decimals everywhere (`5,00`, `0,50`); zero stays blank in project,
   internal and absence rows.
2. Right-align all numeric cells (padding-right ~8 px); headers of week columns
   right-aligned too so labels sit above the digits.
3. One value font size (13 px) and one secondary size (12 px); remove the 11 px Gesamt
   override.

**R2 De-emphasise repetition (mode "Zahlen")**
4. In project rows, a value equal to the previous week's value in the same row renders
   in muted colour (`--alloq-text-muted`); the first value of each run and every change
   render in normal text colour. Compute a boolean `is_repeat` on `GridCell` in the
   builder (pure Python, unit-tested), not in the component.
5. `Arbeitstage (brutto)` header row: show only weeks whose work days differ from the
   standard (5,00 × workload irrelevant here, header is brutto); those values get an
   amber/attention tint. Standard weeks stay blank. Tooltip on the label explains
   "leer = volle Woche".
6. `Interne Projekte` row: show only weeks that differ from the employee's most common
   internal value; the label shows the default, e.g. "Interne Projekte · 0,50/Wo".

**R3 Gesamt row = exceptions only**
7. Colour comes from the free value only (fix #7). Buckets reduce to three visual
   states: `over` (free < 0) → red text **and** light red cell tint; `neutral`
   (free == 0) → muted text, normal weight; `available` (free > 0) → green text,
   normal weight. Keep the sign for non-colour readers.
8. `tight`/`balanced` may stay as backend buckets but map to the 3 visual states.
   Adjust `_gesamt_color` and remove the blue `absent` colour.
9. Weeks with absence get a small calendar-off icon or dot in the Gesamt cell corner
   (not a colour change).
10. Tooltip on each Gesamt cell shows the breakdown:
    "Arbeitstage 5,00 − Projekte 10,00 − Intern 0,50 − Abwesenheit 1,00 = −6,50".
    Data comes from the builder (add fields to `GesamtCell`), not computed in JSX.

**R4 Grid lines & spacing**
11. Remove vertical borders between week cells; keep a faint horizontal line per row
    and a stronger vertical line at month boundaries (add `is_month_start` to
    `WeekColumn`).
12. Replace the 32 px `empty_grid_row()` between employee blocks with an 8 px gap
    (Normal) / 4 px (Kompakt).
13. Current-week highlight stays, applied consistently (background, not the gradient
    hack) across all row types.

**R5 Employee header & collapsed state**
14. Header summary shows exceptions: if any overbooked weeks from current week on,
    "Überbucht X,XX PT in N Wo." in red; else "Frei X,XX PT". Keep "Geplant".
    Extend `employee_summary` (unit-tested).
15. When an employee block is collapsed, its header row renders the Gesamt cells in the
    week columns (same styling as R3), so "Alle einklappen" gives a one-line-per-person
    team overview.

**R6 Display mode "Balken"**
16. New toggle `Zahlen | Balken` (segmented control next to the 3/6/12 Monate control
    in `planning_filter_row.py`), persisted via `rx.LocalStorage`.
17. In "Balken", project cells render a horizontal bar inside the cell: width =
    value / week work days (cap 100 %, overflow shown with a red right edge), colour =
    project colour at ~35 % opacity. Adjacent non-zero weeks visually connect (no
    rounded inner corners) so runs read as one bar. Number hidden; shown on hover
    (title/tooltip) and when the cell is focused/edited.
18. Cells keep all ExcelGrid data attributes; selection, fill handle, copy/paste and
    the overlay editor work unchanged. Gesamt row stays numeric in both modes.

**R7 Density**
19. Toggle `Kompakt | Normal` (icon button in `planning_toolbar.py`), persisted.
    Normal = 32 px rows (today), Kompakt = 24 px rows, 12 px values, week column 52 px.
    `ExcelGrid` uses `ROW_PX = 32` for PageUp/Down — make it tolerate 24 px (read row
    height from the first row instead of the constant).

**R8 Accessibility**
20. Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark (`light-dark(...)` tokens as today).
    Muted repeat text must still pass 4.5:1 on the current-week background.
21. No information conveyed by colour alone (sign, icon, tooltip).

### Deliverables
- Updated `planning_shared.py`, `planning_grid.py`, `planning_project_view.py`
  (shared helpers only), `planning_filter_row.py`, `planning_toolbar.py`.
- New `states/planning_display_mixin.py` (display mode, density, computed style vars),
  mixed into `PlanningStore`.
- Builder changes in `services/planning_builders.py` (`is_repeat`, Gesamt breakdown,
  overbooking summary) and model fields in `states/planning_models.py`.
- `utilization.py`: no change to free-day maths; only if needed a helper mapping bucket
  → visual state.
- Small JSX change in `excel_grid.jsx` for row-height-aware paging.
- Tests:
  - builder: `is_repeat` runs, internal default detection, non-standard work-day weeks,
    Gesamt breakdown text/fields, overbooking summary (extend
    `tests/test_planning_block_summary.py`, `test_planning_grid_rendering.py`).
  - state: display mode / density toggles and persistence defaults
    (new `tests/test_planning_display_mode.py`).
  - rendering: Gesamt colour mapping no longer returns blue for absent+overbooked;
    assert on constants, not rendered umlauts (memory "Reflex render escapes umlauts").

### Success criteria
- `task format && task lint && task typecheck` clean; `task test` green; coverage ≥ 80 %.
- No touched file > 1000 lines (`planning_grid_state.py` must not grow).

## Context

value as a bold-ish `5,00` in a fully ruled grid. With 4 employees and 13 weeks the user
already sees ~250 numbers, most of them identical. Users cannot spot what matters
(overbooking, free capacity, holidays, absences). Goal: the grid stays Excel-editable,
but the eye goes to exceptions first and the repetitive values fade into the background.

User decisions (confirmed):
- Scope: full rework incl. new display modes and density.
- Keep fixed 2 decimals (`5,00`, `0,50`).
- Gesamt row emphasises only exceptions.

---

## Part A — Analysis: what makes the current grid hard to read

Based on established guidance for number-heavy tables (Tufte data-ink ratio; Stephen Few
"Show Me the Numbers" table design; Excel conditional formatting / data bars; resource
planners like Float, Runn, Resource Guru; WCAG 1.4.1 "use of color").

| # | Problem in screenshot | Principle violated | Fix direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Long runs of identical `5,00` per project row; the run's *shape* (start, end, gaps) is the information, not each number | Redundant data ink; preattentive shape beats reading | Data bars / run visualization; repeated values de-emphasised |
| 2 | Every cell has right + bottom border → heavy cage | Non-data ink; gridlines should be barely visible | Drop vertical cell borders, keep faint horizontal lines, stronger month separator only |
| 3 | Numbers centered | Numbers must be right-aligned with tabular figures so decimals line up | Right-align all numeric cells (`tabular-nums` already set) |
| 4 | `Interne Projekte 0,50` repeated in every week for every employee | Constant values carry no information | Show only deviations from the employee's default, or hide by default; fold into Gesamt tooltip |
| 5 | `Arbeitstage (brutto)` header row shows `5,00` 11 times, only holiday weeks matter | Same as 4 | Show only non-standard weeks (e.g. `3,00` highlighted), blank otherwise; or a holiday marker in the week header |
| 6 | Gesamt uses 6 colours (red, violet, 2 greens, blue, black) | Too many hues; no clear meaning | One diverging scheme: red = overbooked, neutral = fully booked, green = free |
| 7 | `absent` bucket paints the value blue even when it is **overbooked** (`-6,50`, `-2,60` blue) | Colour hides the most important exception | Colour from free value only; absence shown separately (icon / hatching in the absence row) |
| 8 | Fully booked weeks `0,00` are bold black → the *ideal* state is the most prominent | Emphasis on the non-exception | Render `0,00` muted (or `✓`/`–`), bold only for exceptions |
| 9 | Signed numbers rely on colour alone (red vs green) | WCAG 1.4.1 | Keep the sign, add a tinted cell background for overbooked cells; tooltip with breakdown |
| 10 | Mixed font sizes (13 px values, 12 px internal, 11 px Gesamt, 11 px headers) | Inconsistent hierarchy | 2 sizes: values 13 px, secondary 12 px; hierarchy via weight/colour, not size |
| 11 | Header summary "Verfügbar 18,50 PT" next to a row full of `-5,50` | Conflicting messages | Header shows exception summary: "Überbucht 44,00 PT in 8 Wo." / "Frei 18,50 PT" |
| 12 | Collapsed employee shows nothing in the week columns | Lost overview | Collapsed header row shows the Gesamt cells inline → one line per person = team overview |
| 13 | 32 px blank spacer row between blocks | Wasted vertical space | 8–12 px gap; block separation via a stronger top border |
| 14 | Week labels `5.10.` without KW | Planners think in KW | Optional `KW 41` with date in tooltip |

colour and weight.** The number is always available (selection, tooltip, edit), but it
does not have to shout in every cell.
